## Which reactions take part (nucleation reactions) {#sec-ch04-nucleation}

### Summary

Only the condensation reactions listed with `type: nucleation` in the YAML input take part in saturation adjustment.
Each one names the formula of its saturation constant. The reader builds the equilibrium stoichiometry from these
reactions and skips every other type, so a condensate produced by a `coagulation` reaction, for example, is never
adjusted (@sec-ch04-conditions). A reaction may also give a temperature range, but no solver uses it.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Choose the reactions and saturation constants of @eq-ch04-conditions-saturation.

**Data.** YAML `reactions:` entries with `type: nucleation` and a `rate-constant:` block.

**Placement.** When the thermodynamics options are read.

**Activation.** `type: nucleation`; `rate-constant: formula` required.

**Guarantee / limits.** Reactants must be gases; `minT`/`maxT` are parsed but unused.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: the reader maps YAML entries to the constants $K_r(T)$ of @sec-ch04-conditions.

### Numerical method

`NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp NucleationOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads each
reaction entry:

1. An entry whose `type`[^rg-e7755bb7941e] is not `nucleation` is skipped.
2. The `equation`[^rg-af50ac18addc] and the `rate-constant`[^rg-f7d3460bb6bb] block are required. In `rate-constant`,
   `formula`[^rg-4090a0a3b182] is required:
   - `ideal` takes `T3`, `P3`, `beta` and `gamma`, with optional `betas` and `gammas` for a solid branch below `T3`;
   - `antoine` takes three coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$, stored as given with no unit conversion, of the curve
     $\log_{10}(p_{\mathrm{sat}}/10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}) = A - B/(T + C)$ (`logsvp_antoine`,
     {{< code src/vapors/vapor_functions.h logsvp_antoine >}}); they are not the Arrhenius factor of the same name
     in @sec-ch06;
   - any other value names a function of the function table, such as `h2o_ideal`, `nh3_ideal` or the two-gas
     `nh3_h2s_lewis` ({{< code src/vapors/vapor_functions.h >}}).
3. `minT` and `maxT` are read, with defaults 0 and $10^4$ K, and are stored. No solver reads them; they appear only in
   the options' printed report (`NucleationOptionsImpl`, {{< code src/thermo/nucleation.hpp NucleationOptionsImpl >}}).
   A temperature range in the input therefore has no effect.

When the species are classified into gases and condensates, a nucleation reactant must be a gas
(`add_to_vapor_cloud`, {{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp add_to_vapor_cloud >}}). Both `ThermoX` and `ThermoY` also
require each nucleation reaction to have a condensed product, when they are built (`ThermoXImpl::reset`,
{{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::reset >}}; `ThermoYImpl::reset`,
{{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}).

| gas/condensate classification | {{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp add_to_vapor_cloud >}} | `add_to_vapor_cloud` | always |

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_saturation_adjustment_nh4sh.py` | two nucleation reactions parsed from YAML are adjusted correctly | RH within $10^{-5}$ | not stated in the test |
| `test_inline_svp.py` | inline `ideal` equals its named twin; `antoine` matches its formula and saturates | bitwise; $10^{-12}$; $10^{-8}$ | bitwise by design; the others not stated in the test |
| `test_thermo.release` | round trips of `ThermoX`/`ThermoY` conversions with the nucleation reactions of `tests/jupiter.yaml` | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not stated in the test |

: Tests of the nucleation reactions. {#tbl-ch04-nucleation-tests}

No test checks that a reaction of another type is excluded, or that `minT`/`maxT` have no effect.

### Limits

- `minT` and `maxT` have no effect, as above.
- A condensate outside every nucleation reaction is not adjusted (@sec-ch04-conditions).

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-e7755bb7941e]: type — name of the rate form; each reader keeps the entries of its own type; required; compared with the reader `name()`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp#L58-L62)

[^rg-af50ac18addc]: equation — reaction string; => irreversible, <=> or = reversible; required; parsed by `Reaction`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp#L64-L68)

[^rg-f7d3460bb6bb]: rate-constant — map of the rate parameters of one reaction entry; read as `rxn_node["rate-constant"]`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp#L76-L79)

[^rg-4090a0a3b182]: formula — name of the saturation vapour pressure function of a nucleation or evaporation entry; required; stored in `logsvp`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/thermo/nucleation.cpp#L68-L72)
